title: 2 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Peter chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Peter Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ
Grace and peace be multiplied unto you
questions.correctAnswer: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Simon Peter identifies himself first in 2 Peter 1:1 before any other statements or commands.

questions.question: Who does Simon Peter identify himself as in 2 Peter 1:1?
options: A servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ
A disciple of John the Baptist
questions.correctAnswer: A servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:1 states Simon Peter is 'a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ.'

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:2, through what are grace and peace multiplied unto you?
options: Through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord
Through the works of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:2 states grace and peace be multiplied through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.

questions.question: What has God's divine power given us according to 2 Peter 1:3?
options: All things that pertain unto life and godliness
questions.correctAnswer: All things that pertain unto life and godliness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:3 says God's divine power hath given us all things that pertain unto life and godliness.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:4, what have believers escaped through the exceeding great and precious promises?
options: The corruption that is in the world through lust
questions.correctAnswer: The corruption that is in the world through lust
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:4 states believers have escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust by the promises.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 1:5, what are you instructed to add to your faith?
questions.correctAnswer: Virtue
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:5 instructs to add virtue to your faith.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:6, which quality comes directly after temperance?
questions.correctAnswer: Patience
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:6 lists patience as the quality that follows temperance.

questions.question: Which is the last quality mentioned in the sequence in 2 Peter 1:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Charity
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:7 ends the sequence with charity.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 1:1 say faith is obtained through?
options: The righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:1 says faith is obtained through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:3, how are we given all things that pertain unto life and godliness?
options: Through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue
Through the sacrifices of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:3 states all things are given through the knowledge of Him who called us to glory and virtue.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:7, what should be added to godliness?
questions.correctAnswer: Brotherly kindness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:7 instructs to add brotherly kindness to godliness.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 1:2 says grace and peace come through the knowledge of God and Jesus our Lord.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:2 explicitly states grace and peace be multiplied through the knowledge of God and Jesus our Lord.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 1:5 instructs believers to give all diligence to add virtue to their faith.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:5 commands giving all diligence to add virtue to faith.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 1:6 says to add joy after temperance.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:6 does not mention joy; it says add patience after temperance.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 1:4 says believers become partakers of the divine nature by observing the law.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:4 says partakers of the divine nature are made so by the exceeding great and precious promises, not by observing the law.

medium.title: 2 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Peter Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:8, what is the result if the qualities mentioned abound in a believer?
options: They shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ
They will be wealthy and powerful in the world
They will never face trials or suffering
questions.correctAnswer: They shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:8 states that if these things be in you and abound, they make you neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 1:10 promise will happen if someone gives diligence to make their calling and election sure as commanded in 2 Peter 1:9?
options: They will be free from all temptation
They will be admired by many
questions.correctAnswer: They shall never fall
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:10 follows 1:9 by urging believers to give diligence to make their calling and election sure, promising that if they do these things, they shall never fall.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 1:9 say about a person who lacks the qualities mentioned in the prior verses?
options: He is blind and cannot see afar off, and has forgotten that he was purged from his old sins
He is weak but will be strengthened soon
He is chosen but not yet fully saved
He is more humble than others
questions.correctAnswer: He is blind and cannot see afar off, and has forgotten that he was purged from his old sins
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:9 clearly states that the person who lacks these things is blind and cannot see afar off, and has forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 1:11 relate to the diligence encouraged in 2 Peter 1:10?
options: It promises an abundant entrance into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ
It warns that diligence may lead to persecution
It encourages giving more money to the church
It states that diligence is unnecessary for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It promises an abundant entrance into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:11 explains that because of the diligence encouraged in verse 10, an abundant entrance into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ will be ministered.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:12, why does Peter say he will not be negligent in reminding believers of these truths?
options: Because they already know them and are established in the present truth
Because they are new believers and need constant teaching
Because he wants to gain authority over them
questions.correctAnswer: Because they already know them and are established in the present truth
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:12 states that Peter will not be negligent to remind them of these things because they know them and are established in the present truth.

questions.question: What is Peter’s reason for stirring up believers by putting them in remembrance, according to 2 Peter 1:13?
options: Because he thinks it is fitting as long as he is in this tabernacle
Because they are forgetting the gospel
Because he wants to write another letter
Because he is planning to visit them soon
questions.correctAnswer: Because he thinks it is fitting as long as he is in this tabernacle
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:13 explains that Peter thinks it is meet to stir them up by putting them in remembrance while he is still in this tabernacle (his earthly body).

questions.question: What impending event does Peter acknowledge in 2 Peter 1:14?
options: That shortly he must put off his tabernacle, similar to the Lord Jesus Christ
That he will travel to another city
That he will write another epistle
questions.correctAnswer: That shortly he must put off his tabernacle, similar to the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:14 states that Peter knows he must shortly put off this tabernacle, meaning his earthly body, just as the Lord Jesus Christ showed him.

questions.question: What qualities does Peter instruct believers to add to their faith in 2 Peter 1:5-7?
options: Virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, charity
questions.correctAnswer: Virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, charity
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:5-7 lists these specific qualities for believers to add to their faith in order to grow spiritually.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:4, what have believers escaped through the precious promises given to them?
options: The corruption that is in the world through lust
questions.correctAnswer: The corruption that is in the world through lust
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:4 explains that believers, through great and precious promises, have escaped the corruption in the world caused by lust.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 1:2 describe the way grace and peace are multiplied to believers?
options: Through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:2 states that grace and peace are multiplied unto believers through the knowledge of God and Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What has divine power given to believers according to 2 Peter 1:3?
options: All things that pertain unto life and godliness
questions.correctAnswer: All things that pertain unto life and godliness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:3 explains that God's divine power has given believers all things that pertain to life and godliness through the knowledge of Him.

questions.question: What practical Christian living result is linked to the qualities abounding in a believer in 2 Peter 1:8?
options: They become fruitful in the knowledge of Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: They become fruitful in the knowledge of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:8 states that if these qualities abound in a believer, they make him neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What warning is given in 2 Peter 1:9 about lacking the qualities mentioned?
options: He is blind and cannot see afar off
He will be rejected by the church
questions.correctAnswer: He is blind and cannot see afar off
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:9 warns that he who lacks these qualities is blind and cannot see afar off, indicating spiritual shortsightedness.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 1:14 indicates that Peter knew he would soon die as Jesus Christ had shown him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:14 states that Peter knew shortly he must put off this tabernacle, just as the Lord Jesus Christ had shown him, indicating his awareness of impending death.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Peter 1:10, believers who make their calling and election sure will eventually fall.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:10 clearly states that if believers do these things, they shall never fall.

hard.title: 2 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Peter Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:15, what does Peter endeavor to ensure after his decease?
options: That the readers may have these things always in remembrance
That the readers receive financial blessings
That the readers conquer their enemies
That the readers build a church
questions.correctAnswer: That the readers may have these things always in remembrance
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:15 states that Peter will endeavor so that after his death, the readers may always remember these things.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 1:16, what is the basis of Peter's proclamation about the power and coming of Jesus Christ?
options: They were eyewitnesses of his majesty
They relied on oral tradition only
questions.correctAnswer: They were eyewitnesses of his majesty
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:16 emphasizes that Peter and others were eyewitnesses of Jesus' majesty, not followers of cunningly devised fables.

questions.question: What event does 2 Peter 1:17 describe where Jesus received honor and glory?
options: When a voice came from the excellent glory saying, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased'
When Jesus was baptized by John
When Jesus performed the miracle of feeding the 5000
questions.correctAnswer: When a voice came from the excellent glory saying, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased'
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:17 records that Jesus received honor and glory when God the Father spoke from excellent glory, declaring Jesus as His beloved Son.

questions.question: Where were Peter and the other apostles when they heard the voice from heaven as recorded in 2 Peter 1:18?
questions.correctAnswer: In the holy mount
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:18 states that the voice from heaven was heard while they were with Jesus on the holy mount.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:19, how is the word of prophecy described?
options: A more sure word of prophecy, like a light shining in a dark place
questions.correctAnswer: A more sure word of prophecy, like a light shining in a dark place
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:19 describes prophecy as a more sure word, likened to a light shining in a dark place until the day dawns.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 1:20 teach about the interpretation of prophecy in scripture?
options: No prophecy of scripture is of any private interpretation
Each person may interpret prophecy as they wish
questions.correctAnswer: No prophecy of scripture is of any private interpretation
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:20 clearly states that prophecy does not come from private interpretation but from God’s will.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'prophetes' (προφήτης) in 2 Peter 1:21 mean?
options: One who speaks forth God's message
questions.correctAnswer: One who speaks forth God's message
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'prophetes' means one who speaks forth God’s message, as used in 2 Peter 1:21 about holy men moved by the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Peter 1:19 when describing prophecy as a 'light that shineth in a dark place'?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:19 uses a simile comparing prophecy to a light shining in a dark place, using 'as unto' to make the comparison explicit.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to 2 Peter 1:17’s voice from heaven declaring Jesus as the beloved Son?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 2:7
questions.explanation: Psalm 2:7 speaks of God declaring His Son, which connects thematically to the voice in 2 Peter 1:17 declaring Jesus as God's beloved Son.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the teaching in 2 Peter 1:21 about prophecy not coming by the will of man but by the Holy Spirit?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Timothy 3:16
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 3:16 affirms that all Scripture is God-breathed, echoing 2 Peter 1:21’s teaching on prophecy through the Holy Spirit, not human will.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 2 Peter 1:16 in the chapter?
options: Peter’s declaration to not be negligent in reminding the readers
The description of adding virtue and knowledge to faith
questions.correctAnswer: Peter’s declaration to not be negligent in reminding the readers
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:15 states Peter’s resolve to remind the readers after his death, which immediately precedes verse 16.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 1:21, what is the significance of the phrase 'holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost'?
options: It emphasizes divine inspiration as the source of prophecy
It suggests prophecy was a human invention
It means prophets spoke only their own opinions
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes divine inspiration as the source of prophecy
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:21 highlights that prophecy is inspired by the Holy Spirit, not human will, affirming divine origin.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 1:19 serve as an inclusio with the earlier parts of the chapter?
options: By framing prophecy as a guiding light, linking eyewitness testimony to the enduring word
By repeating the same phrase twice
By introducing a new topic unrelated to the rest
questions.correctAnswer: By framing prophecy as a guiding light, linking eyewitness testimony to the enduring word
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:19 uses the metaphor of light in darkness, creating an inclusio that connects the eyewitness accounts with the lasting prophetic word.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 1:16-18, what is the purpose of Peter’s emphasis on being eyewitnesses of Jesus' majesty?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:16-18 stresses eyewitness testimony to disprove cunningly devised fables, affirming the reality of Jesus' majesty.

questions.question: 2 Peter 1:20 states that prophecy of scripture is subject to private interpretation.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:20 explicitly states that no prophecy of scripture is of any private interpretation, negating individualistic readings.

theological.title: 2 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Peter Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 1:4 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation includes becoming partakers of the divine nature, escaping world corruption through lust
Salvation is solely a legal declaration of righteousness
Salvation is based on human effort and moral achievement
Salvation depends on adherence to ceremonial law
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation includes becoming partakers of the divine nature, escaping world corruption through lust
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:4 states that believers are given great and precious promises so that they may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption in the world through lust, which teaches the doctrine of salvation as transformation and participation in God's nature.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 1:21 teach about the inspiration of Scripture?
options: Prophecy came by men moved by the Holy Ghost, not by human will
Prophecy is primarily a product of human imagination
Scripture is a collection of private interpretations
Prophecy is dictated by cultural circumstances alone
questions.correctAnswer: Prophecy came by men moved by the Holy Ghost, not by human will
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:21 clearly states that prophecy did not come by the will of man but by holy men of God who spoke as they were moved by the Holy Ghost, teaching the doctrine of divine inspiration of Scripture.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 1:10 teach about assurance of salvation?
options: Believers are exhorted to give diligence to make their calling and election sure
Assurance of salvation cannot be known in this life
Election is a secret that should not be pursued
Salvation is guaranteed regardless of Christian growth
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are exhorted to give diligence to make their calling and election sure
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:10 exhorts believers to make their calling and election sure by practicing godly virtues, teaching that assurance of salvation involves active diligence in sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Peter 1:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:3 speaks of God's divine power giving us all things pertaining to life and godliness through His calling, demonstrating God's sovereignty in salvation and provision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Peter 1:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Grace
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:2 speaks of grace and peace being multiplied through knowledge of God and Jesus, highlighting the divine attribute of grace extended to believers.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 1:16–18 connect to the broader New Testament theme of Christ’s exaltation?
options: By affirming Christ's majesty witnessed on the Mount of Transfiguration
By focusing solely on Christ’s earthly ministry
questions.correctAnswer: By affirming Christ's majesty witnessed on the Mount of Transfiguration
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:16–18 recounts eyewitness testimony of Christ’s majesty and the voice from heaven, connecting to the New Testament theme of Christ’s exaltation after resurrection.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 1:19’s emphasis on prophecy as a light in darkness relate to Old Testament themes?
options: It echoes the prophetic hope for a coming Messiah as light in darkness
It asserts that prophecy is irrelevant for Christians
It denies any continuity with the Old Testament
It claims prophecy is only symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the prophetic hope for a coming Messiah as light in darkness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:19 likens prophecy to a light shining in a dark place until the day dawns, resonating with Old Testament messianic prophecies about coming light and salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 1:5 and 1:7 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves adding virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and charity
Sanctification is instantaneous without progressive growth
Sanctification is only external behavior modification
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves adding virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and charity
questions.explanation: Verses 1:5 and 1:7 list a progression of godly qualities to be added to faith, teaching that sanctification is a process of growth in multiple virtues.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 1:9 and 1:10 teach about spiritual discernment and perseverance?
options: Lacking godly virtues results in spiritual blindness and jeopardizes assurance of salvation
Spiritual discernment is unrelated to perseverance
Assurance is automatic regardless of spiritual growth
Blindness is only physical and not spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: Lacking godly virtues results in spiritual blindness and jeopardizes assurance of salvation
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:9 warns that the one lacking these virtues is blind and forgets cleansing from sins, while 1:10 urges diligence to confirm calling and election, linking discernment with perseverance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Peter 1:20 and 1:21 teach about biblical prophecy and its interpretation?
options: No prophecy is private interpretation; it originates from men moved by the Holy Spirit
Prophecy is primarily human opinion open to individual interpretation
Prophecy is dictated by political agendas
questions.correctAnswer: No prophecy is private interpretation; it originates from men moved by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Verses 1:20 and 1:21 teach that Scripture prophecy is not from private interpretation but from holy men of God inspired by the Holy Spirit, affirming the divine origin and objective authority of prophecy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Peter 1:16–18 is based on cunningly devised fables with no eyewitness basis. What does 2 Peter 1:16–18 actually teach?
options: The testimony is from eyewitnesses who witnessed the majesty and heard the voice from heaven
The passage admits it is a myth
The passage is a secondhand report without eyewitnesses
It is a fictional story meant to inspire
questions.correctAnswer: The testimony is from eyewitnesses who witnessed the majesty and heard the voice from heaven
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:16–18 asserts that the apostles did not follow fables but were eyewitnesses of Christ’s majesty and heard the voice from heaven, affirming historical reliability.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 1:6 teach about the role of temperance in spiritual growth?
options: Temperance is a necessary virtue to be added to knowledge and followed by patience
Temperance is optional and unrelated to other virtues
Temperance is merely self-denial without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Temperance is a necessary virtue to be added to knowledge and followed by patience
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:6 instructs believers to add temperance to knowledge and then patience, emphasizing temperance as an integral step in spiritual development.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Peter 1:17 specifically demonstrate through the voice from the excellent glory?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine approval and glory
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:17 records God the Father giving honor and glory to the Son with a voice declaring 'This is my beloved Son,' demonstrating divine approval and glory.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 1:14–15 prepare the church for apostolic succession and doctrinal remembrance?
options: By the apostle's intent to remind believers after his death to remain steadfast
By commanding immediate cessation of teaching
By denying the need for doctrinal continuity
By encouraging the abandonment of apostolic teaching
questions.correctAnswer: By the apostle's intent to remind believers after his death to remain steadfast
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:14–15 shows Peter’s awareness of his impending death and his commitment to leave a reminder for the church to uphold truth, preparing for doctrinal continuity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 1:11 teach about the believer's ultimate destiny?
options: Believers will receive entrance abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of Jesus Christ
Believers will experience temporary reward only
questions.correctAnswer: Believers will receive entrance abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 1:11 promises that those who grow in godliness will be granted abundant entrance into Christ’s eternal kingdom, teaching the doctrine of eternal inheritance.
